nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on an arbitrary vertex set that has no proper colouring with finitely many colours. Then the family $(1/\ell)$, indexed by the odd cycle lengths $\ell$ of $G$ (the odd numbers $\ell$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$), is not summable; that is, $\sum_\ell 1/\ell = \infty$.
nodes.title: Odd cycle lengths and infinite chromatic number (Erdős Problem 57)

nodes.summary: The proposition that every simple graph $G$ with infinite chromatic number has cycles of length $2^n$ for infinitely many $n$: for every natural number $N$ there is some $n \ge N$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $2^n$.

nodes.summary: It is not the case that both of the following hold: (i) for every natural number $k$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$; (ii) for all natural numbers $k$ and $g$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ and girth at least $g$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 751 is false
